## Design

### 2026-10-27: Day 1 Week 4 - Beginnings

**3h**

Day 1 Week 4 - Beginnings

Today I conceptualized and created the first schematic of Pixxcraft. I decided to make a simple (kinda) project this time, just a little keychain-sized thingy where you can paint an image like MS Paint, and apply simple animations like scrolling pixels, fading, or sizing up/down, otherwise you can hand-draw them. Keep in mind they aren't supposed to be like full-on animations, just simple GIFs, like wind blowing or smoke coming out of the chimney of a house drawing.

Concept (my amazing drawing skills show here):
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/eb82e20a55bba2f1de3c77b5b57140cf9a063843d56211e8e3099eca5cb45d7a.png)

Next, I looked for a good TFT color touchscreen, or at least a footprint/schematic for one. For now, I'm going to use a Connector, 01x12, to be specific. I wired up the pins and then to the ESP32-S3, which will be the main brains of this project.

The wired up TFT:

![Screenshot 2026-10-26 234821](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/fec2908c859cf31604cf70f4d18c4d2acbdb29531b8a2b6a75c35e4c1f2fd416.png)

Finally, the way I want to go forward with this project is software. The screen I might be using already has a library, I'm going to use that and write the code for it. Perhaps I could make it stylus compatible, for the real artists? Right now, this project doesn't have too much ambition, especially since I have 2 pins left after adding the TFT.

Day 1 final progress:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 214524](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/2d105dc54d7869a923b74e1f6e79fc99c13ceafe998a27e8308936218741f4f1.png)

### 2026-10-28: Day 2 Week 4

**3h**

Day 2 Week 4

The schematic and PCB are finished, and it wasn't as hard as compared to my other projects. I started off from last time with the proper schematic, and started assigning footprints. I gave the ESP-32-S3 the corresponding footprint, and then the connector, meant to represent the OLED, as initially a PinHeader. I imported the schematic into the PCB and then realized, which screen am I using? Because a TFT touchscreen is not a drag-and-drop replaceable component.

The PCB, with the wrong footprint:

![Screenshot 2026-10-27 222319](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/9ebb025ae5ebb754097e65697f569e54b18fb6d45dcac673f9764049198797b0.png)

Next, I began to do some research on which screen I wanted to use, which one I would build the board around. After looking through many options, I settled on this one on WaveShare. https://www.waveshare.com/product/1.69inch-touch-lcd-module.htm
I changed the connector footprint to a JST connector, with the matching specifications for the screen.

Screen:
![1.69inch-touch-lcd-module-5](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/9800f050637e8a3d9db8ce4e136e81255e0e529299f172ec63cb09aedff05777.jpg)

Finally, I finished the board, adding traces with my experience (and partially PTSD) from my previous projects. I even added a little hole in the board to put it on a keychain or something. The board is mostly complete, save for some minor adjustments I might need to make. At this time, I began work on programming. I used AI to code up a simulator using SDL2 for which I would test my code in. Keep in mind, I will be writing the actual code myself, the simulator is for errors and debugging.

Final result:
